source.title: Refusal geometry reflects refusal training: diverse refusal prefixes can raise stable rank and weaken refusal vector ablation attacks

record.tranche_reason: The study varies refusal-completion first-token diversity and measures activation stable rank and the effect of a refusal-vector ablation. This conceptually tests whether refusal-training data can shape a concentrated refusal mechanism, but it does not measure the response-position KL or the fine-tuning, prefilling, suffix, or decoding interventions in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports checkpoint comparisons, gradient and activation-update ranks, subspace overlaps, cross-layer transfer factors, and shared-map fits. These do not directly measure the listed claim versions except insofar as refusal-start diversity is used to test the data-source explanation in V6. The paper cites prior work on early-token safety concentration; those cited results are not recorded here.
record.test_reason: The study measures activation-space stable rank of refusal residuals and vulnerability to a difference-in-means single-vector ablation. It varies refusal first-token diversity in one OLMo-2 1B model. It never measures where safety sits across response positions (no per-token KL, no prefilling, suffixes or decoding attacks), harmful-compliance after harmful or benign fine-tuning, parameter-level localization, or a deepening objective. It links refusal-prefix concentration in the data to a related construct, low-rank refusal geometry, rather than to positional shallowness. So it does not test V6 or any other version; Qi et al. appear only as cited related work. The finding goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that refusal directions in OLMo-2-0425-1B-Instruct reflect first-token refusal-training gradients, and that repeated refusal first tokens yield low-stable-rank activation changes that are easier to ablate with one vector. Diversifying refusal starts raises stable rank and is associated with smaller ablation deltas: slight in the frozen-model subsets, clearer in controlled fine-tuning. They say it is unlikely to be a complete defense on its own.
record.recipe_differences: Varies refusal-completion first-token diversity, measures activation-space stable rank, and tests difference-in-means activation ablation. It does not reproduce harmful-example fine-tuning safety-loss results or measure per-response-position KL; the controlled training uses 40 benign chemistry prompts paired with sampled refusals.
record.method_sensitivity: The rank–ablation relationship is examined at layer 7 in the frozen-model analysis and layer 8 in controlled fine-tuning. The controlled fine-tuning selects checkpoints at the first refusal rate of at least 0.6; the authors report that ablation effect varies over optimization steps.

fits_no_version.finding: In OLMo-2-0425-1B-Instruct, more diverse refusal first tokens raise the stable rank of refusal residuals and gradients. Higher rank goes with smaller single-vector ablation refusal deltas: slight in frozen subsets (Fig. 9, about 0.74 to 0.60), larger in controlled fine-tuning (Fig. 11, about 0.60 to 0.30; Fig. 22 peak deltas 0.55 at 8 starts vs 0.375 at 16). Harm deltas also shrink with rank (Fig. 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concentrated refusal prefixes (repeated first tokens) in refusal-training data produce a low-rank refusal representation that is more vulnerable to single-direction activation ablation.

record.problems: The study is primarily a case study of one small OLMo model family, English-language data, and relatively small prompt sets. The frozen-model attack estimates and applies a direction on the same prompt set, so held-out transfer is not established. The controlled fine-tuning uses effective batch size one and first-token-only loss; the authors note that the measurements omit later completion-token gradients and ordinary minibatch and optimizer interactions. The key stable-rank and refusal-delta values in the cited figures are not numerically stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted ancillary target-matrix and raw-gradient stable-rank plots, gradient-induced update ranks, checkpoint comparisons, subspace-overlap results, and shared-map diagnostics (Sections 4.2-4.4, Figures 2-4, 6-7, 12-23). These do not directly measure the listed claim versions beyond the refusal-residual rank and ablation outcomes retained above.

untested.parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning or measure of harmful compliance.
No benign fine-tuning followed by a harmful-compliance evaluation. The chemistry fine-tuning trains refusals, not compliance.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
No prefilling, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes. Only difference-in-means activation ablation.
No weight- or parameter-rank localization. Only activation-space stable rank.
Does not measure whether safety concentrates in early response positions, or whether the data or objective causes such positional concentration.
No training that spreads safety across positions; no robustness evaluation against fine-tuning or prefill attacks.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'tested' status and its supports labels are removed. V6 concerns why safety is shallow across response positions, and this study never measures positional depth. Its construct, activation-direction rank and ablation vulnerability, is related but different. Ablation attacks use the same prompt set for estimating and applying the direction; the study covers one 1B model, English data and small prompt sets.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred harmful examples or measurement of harmful-request compliance after such fine-tuning.
No ordinary or carefully selected benign instruction fine-tuning followed by a harmful-compliance evaluation.
No per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes. Difference-in-means activation ablation is studied, but it is not one of the interventions named in this version.
The study measures activation-space stable rank and single-vector ablation, not whether a small set of model weights or parameter ranks carries safety behavior.

Tests whether refusal-start diversity in the training data affects activation rank and single-vector ablation in the studied setting. It does not test whether the model's safety-related output distribution is concentrated in the first few response positions, nor does it establish the explanation across models or training objectives.
No training objective that spreads safety across response positions, or evaluation of robustness to fine-tuning, prefilling, suffixes, or decoding changes.

rows.subject: allenai/OLMo-2-0425-1B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Measured stable rank of benign-centered refusal residuals across subsets with varied refusal-start support.
rows.measure: Stable rank of refusal residual matrix ΔH
rows.note: The text says stable rank rises as refusal-start diversity increases; this is the one-start setting, and its plotted value is not stated numerically.
rows.check: Stable rank of benign-centered activation residuals is not a measure of positional safety depth or of data causing shallowness. Values are figure-only; axes span about 1.6-2.2 averaged over layers 7-15 (Fig. 5).

rows.note: The text says refusal delta decreases slightly as residual stable rank rises; plotted value for this condition is not stated numerically.
rows.check: The refusal delta under difference-in-means activation ablation is a white-box activation attack, not a prefill, suffix or decoding attack (V4), and it does not measure positional shallowness. Fig. 9 shows deltas of only about 0.74 to 0.60 across subsets; the authors call the decrease slight.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Frozen OLMo-2-0425-1B-Instruct on WildJailbreak training-split subsets
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that increasing refusal-start diversity raises refusal-residual stable rank and slightly reduces refusal-ablation delta (R1-R18).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Controlled refusal fine-tuning of OLMo-2-0425-1B-Instruct on CAMEL chemistry prompts, checkpoints matched at refusal rate 0.6
reader_labels.reason: The authors report higher residual stable rank and smaller single-vector ablation deltas with more refusal-start buckets (R19-R28).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The study's tested model and data settings
reader_labels.reason: This is a one-model, English-language case study; the authors say refusal-completion diversity alone is unlikely to be a complete defense, and they do not test output-position KL or safety depth (R1-R28).
